title: What is competency-based training?
description: Competency-based training (CBT) trains and assesses people against defined workplace standards, not hours. How it works, with a worked example.
shortAnswer: A competency-based training (CBT) system is an approach in which learners are trained and assessed against defined workplace standards, and are judged competent when they can show they meet those standards, rather than when they have spent a set amount of time in a course. Many national vocational systems use this model; US Registered Apprenticeship programs, for example, may measure progress by demonstrated competency rather than hours.
keyTakeaways: Competency-based training focuses on what a person can do at the workplace standard, not on hours of attendance or a ranked grade.
In national vocational systems, the standards are published occupational standards, such as units of competency or the competencies described in apprenticeship program standards.
Assessment results are typically competent or not yet competent, supported by evidence against the unit's requirements.

Regulated systems add formal rules, such as the competency-based option in US Registered Apprenticeship standards or the principles of assessment and rules of evidence set by vocational regulators such as ASQA.

blocks.text: Competency-based training works by starting from a defined standard of workplace performance, teaching toward it, and then collecting evidence that the learner meets it.

items: **Define the standard.** A unit of competency, or an internal [competency framework](/glossary/competency-framework), describes the task, the performance criteria and the knowledge required.
**Recognize what the learner already has.** [Recognition of prior learning](/glossary/recognition-of-prior-learning) can credit existing competence so training time is not wasted.
**Train to the gap.** Instruction and practice target the parts of the standard the learner cannot yet meet.
**Assess against the standard.** A [competency assessment](/glossary/competency-assessment) gathers performance and knowledge evidence.
**Record the decision.** The learner is judged competent or not yet competent, with the evidence retained.

sections.heading: How is competency-based training used in national vocational systems?

blocks.text: Competency-based training is the basis of many national vocational systems. In the United States, federal standards for Registered Apprenticeship let a program measure the term of apprenticeship by hours, by "the attainment of competency (competency-based approach)", or by a hybrid of the two. A competency-based program must still include on the job learning, describe its competencies and identify how each is tested ([29 CFR 29.5(b)(2)](https://www.ecfr.gov/current/title-29/subtitle-A/part-29/section-29.5)).

Vocational regulators often publish the assessment rules. For example, the Australian Skills Quality Authority (ASQA) [assessment practice guide](https://www.asqa.gov.au/for-providers/standards-for-RTOs/practice-guides/quality-area-1-training-and-assessment/assessment-practice-guide) states that Standard 1.4 of the 2025 Standards for Registered Training Organisations requires assessment to follow the principles of fairness, flexibility, validity and reliability, and assessor judgments to meet the rules of evidence: validity, sufficiency, authenticity and currency. The details are covered in [Standards for RTOs 2025: training and assessment](/regulations/standards-for-rtos-2025-training-and-assessment).

Employers outside formal vocational systems use the same model for internal programs, particularly in safety critical and regulated roles, where the question a regulator asks is whether the worker can do the task safely, not whether they attended a session.

sections.heading: What does competency-based training look like for one task?

blocks.text: Illustrative example: a logistics business uses nationally endorsed units, delivered through an accredited training provider, for general equipment operation. For site specific tasks that no national unit covers, such as its own dangerous goods segregation rules, it writes an internal competency with the same structure.

items: **Standard:** segregates incompatible dangerous goods classes according to the site segregation chart.
**Performance evidence:** correctly segregates three mixed loads under observation.
**Knowledge evidence:** explains the segregation chart and the incident reporting step.
**Result:** competent, with observation checklist and knowledge responses retained; a learner who errs on one load is not yet competent and receives targeted practice.

sections.heading: How does Knowledge Foundry approach this?

blocks.text: Knowledge Foundry structures internal competencies the way national vocational systems structure units of competency: requirement, performance evidence and knowledge evidence, each linked to a source. Training content and assessments are then generated against that structure rather than written first.

faqs.q: Is competency-based training the same as nationally recognized training?
faqs.a: No. Competency-based describes how training is designed and assessed; national recognition describes who may issue the credential. Recognized qualifications are normally issued only by accredited providers against official standards. Employers can run their own competency-based programs, but those programs do not by themselves produce recognized credentials.

faqs.q: Why are results competent or not yet competent rather than grades?
faqs.a: Because the question is whether the learner meets the workplace standard. A graded scale implies degrees of passing, but in competency-based training a person either meets the standard with sufficient evidence or does not yet meet it. Some providers add graded feedback, but the competency decision itself is binary.

faqs.q: Does competency-based training still have a minimum duration?
faqs.a: Competency is not granted for time served, but time still matters. Learners need sufficient time for instruction, practice, feedback and assessment. US Registered Apprenticeship rules reflect this: a program using the competency-based approach must still require apprentices to complete an on the job learning component.

faqs.q: Can competency-based training be used for compliance topics?
faqs.a: Yes, and it is often a better fit than completion based e-learning. Writing the compliance obligation as a performance standard, such as correctly handling a scenario, gives evidence that people can apply the rule, which is closer to what regulators test after an incident.
